## Bokeh Examples {#sec-bokeh-examples}

**maidr** also supports **Bokeh** figures and layouts. Pass a `figure`, a
`gridplot`, or a `row`/`column` of figures to `maidr.show()`, `maidr.render()`
or `maidr.save_html()`, and **maidr** produces a page where the interactive
Bokeh plot keeps its pan, zoom and hover tools and can also be read from the
keyboard, as sound, as text and in braille. For the other libraries, see the
[Matplotlib / Seaborn](examples.qmd), [Plotly](examples-plotly.qmd) and
[Altair](examples-altair.qmd) pages.

::: {.callout-warning title="Experimental"}
Bokeh support is **experimental**. What it reads, and how, may change without a
deprecation period, whichever plot type is drawn: see
[Plot Type Stability](stability.qmd#bokeh-support). Install it with
`pip install "maidr[bokeh]"`.
:::

**maidr** reads the figure's own renderers and data sources, not the drawn
canvas, so what you hear is the data you plotted. As you move through a chart
the mark being read is highlighted in the Bokeh plot itself: a bar, bin, cell,
slice, candle or point is selected, dimming the rest, and a line, step or area shows a ring
on the current point. A bar, bin, cell or point whose data source another mark
also draws from, such as markers on a line built from one `ColumnDataSource`,
gets the ring too, so the other mark is never faded.

| Bokeh | read as |
|---|---|
| `vbar`, `hbar` | bar |
| `vbar_stack`, `hbar_stack` | stacked bar |
| `vbar` with `dodge()` or an offset such as `("a", -0.2)`, or on a nested `FactorRange` | dodged bar |
| `quad` | histogram |
| `line`, `multi_line` | line, one series per renderer or path |
| `step` | step |
| `scatter`, `circle` | point |
| `rect` coloured through a continuous colour mapper (`linear_cmap`, `log_cmap`) | heatmap |
| `wedge`, `annular_wedge` | pie, one slice per row |
| `segment` wicks with `vbar` bodies on a datetime axis (Bokeh's OHLC recipe) | candlestick |
| `varea`, `varea_stack`, `harea`, `harea_stack` | area [experimental], stacked area [experimental] |
| `hbar` from one date to another (`left=start`, `right=end` on a datetime axis) | gantt [experimental] |
| `hex_tile` coloured through a colour mapper, as `p.hexbin` draws it | hexbin [experimental] |

Any other glyph is left out with a warning naming it, and a figure with nothing
**maidr** can read is still drawn. A `Tabs` layout is read one panel at a time:
the active one.

### Bar Plot

```{python}
#| warning: false
#| fig-alt: Bar chart showing average body mass of penguins by species

import seaborn as sns
from bokeh.plotting import figure

import maidr  #<<

penguins = sns.load_dataset("penguins")
avg_mass = penguins.groupby("species")["body_mass_g"].mean()
species = avg_mass.index.tolist()

p = figure(
    x_range=species,
    title="Average Body Mass of Penguins by Species",
    x_axis_label="Species",
    y_axis_label="Body Mass (g)",
    height=350,
)
p.vbar(x=species, top=avg_mass.round(1).tolist(), width=0.8, color="#4c72b0")

maidr.show(p)  #<<
```

### Horizontal Bar Plot

```{python}
#| warning: false
#| fig-alt: Horizontal bar chart of the number of penguins on each island

import seaborn as sns
from bokeh.plotting import figure

import maidr  #<<

penguins = sns.load_dataset("penguins")
counts = penguins["island"].value_counts().sort_values()

p = figure(
    y_range=counts.index.tolist(),
    title="Penguins Counted on Each Island",
    x_axis_label="Penguins",
    y_axis_label="Island",
    height=300,
)
p.hbar(y=counts.index.tolist(), right=counts.tolist(), height=0.7, color="#55a868")

maidr.show(p)  #<<
```

### Stacked Bar Plot

```{python}
#| warning: false
#| fig-alt: Stacked bar chart of total restaurant bills by day, split by sex

import seaborn as sns
from bokeh.plotting import figure

import maidr  #<<

tips = sns.load_dataset("tips")
totals = tips.pivot_table(
    index="day", columns="sex", values="total_bill", aggfunc="sum", observed=True
)
days = [str(day) for day in totals.index]
source = {"day": days, "Male": totals["Male"].round(2), "Female": totals["Female"].round(2)}

p = figure(
    x_range=days,
    title="Total Bill by Day and Sex",
    x_axis_label="Day",
    y_axis_label="Total Bill ($)",
    height=350,
)
p.vbar_stack(
    ["Male", "Female"],
    x="day",
    width=0.8,
    source=source,
    color=["#4c72b0", "#dd8452"],
    legend_label=["Male", "Female"],
)
p.legend.title = "Sex"

maidr.show(p)  #<<
```

### Dodged (Grouped) Bar Plot

```{python}
#| warning: false
#| fig-alt: Grouped bar chart comparing average body mass by species and sex

import seaborn as sns
from bokeh.models import ColumnDataSource
from bokeh.plotting import figure
from bokeh.transform import dodge

import maidr  #<<

penguins = sns.load_dataset("penguins").dropna()
by_sex = penguins.pivot_table(
    index="species", columns="sex", values="body_mass_g", aggfunc="mean"
).round(1)
species = by_sex.index.tolist()
source = ColumnDataSource(
    {"species": species, "Male": by_sex["Male"], "Female": by_sex["Female"]}
)

p = figure(
    x_range=species,
    title="Average Body Mass by Species and Sex",
    x_axis_label="Species",
    y_axis_label="Body Mass (g)",
    height=350,
)
p.vbar(
    x=dodge("species", -0.2, range=p.x_range), top="Male", width=0.35,
    source=source, color="#4c72b0", legend_label="Male",
)
p.vbar(
    x=dodge("species", 0.2, range=p.x_range), top="Female", width=0.35,
    source=source, color="#dd8452", legend_label="Female",
)
p.legend.title = "Sex"

maidr.show(p)  #<<
```

A `vbar` on a nested `FactorRange` -- `x=[("Adelie", "Male"), ("Adelie",
"Female"), ...]` -- is read the same way: the inner factor names the group,
and the outer one the category.

### Histogram

```{python}
#| warning: false
#| fig-alt: Histogram of penguin flipper lengths

import numpy as np
import seaborn as sns
from bokeh.plotting import figure

import maidr  #<<

penguins = sns.load_dataset("penguins").dropna()
counts, edges = np.histogram(penguins["flipper_length_mm"], bins=12)

p = figure(
    title="Distribution of Penguin Flipper Length",
    x_axis_label="Flipper Length (mm)",
    y_axis_label="Count",
    height=350,
)
p.quad(
    top=counts, bottom=0, left=edges[:-1], right=edges[1:],
    fill_color="#8172b3", line_color="white",
)

maidr.show(p)  #<<
```

### Line Plot

```{python}
#| warning: false
#| fig-alt: Line chart of total airline passengers per year

import seaborn as sns
from bokeh.plotting import figure

import maidr  #<<

flights = sns.load_dataset("flights")
per_year = flights.groupby("year")["passengers"].sum()

p = figure(
    title="Airline Passengers per Year",
    x_axis_label="Year",
    y_axis_label="Passengers",
    height=350,
)
p.line(per_year.index.tolist(), per_year.tolist(), line_width=2)

maidr.show(p)  #<<
```

### Multi-Line Plot

```{python}
#| warning: false
#| fig-alt: Three lines comparing monthly passengers in 1949, 1954 and 1960

import seaborn as sns
from bokeh.plotting import figure

import maidr  #<<

flights = sns.load_dataset("flights")

p = figure(
    title="Monthly Passengers in Three Years",
    x_axis_label="Month",
    y_axis_label="Passengers",
    height=350,
)
for year, color in [(1949, "#4c72b0"), (1954, "#55a868"), (1960, "#c44e52")]:
    rows = flights[flights["year"] == year]
    p.line(
        list(range(1, 13)), rows["passengers"].tolist(),
        line_width=2, color=color, legend_label=str(year),
    )
p.legend.title = "Year"
p.legend.location = "top_left"

maidr.show(p)  #<<
```

Every `line` on a figure becomes one series of one line layer, named by its
legend label; press the up and down arrows to move between them.

### Step Plot

```{python}
#| warning: false
#| fig-alt: Step chart of the largest single bill seen so far by table

import seaborn as sns
from bokeh.plotting import figure

import maidr  #<<

tips = sns.load_dataset("tips").head(20)
running_max = tips["total_bill"].cummax()

p = figure(
    title="Largest Bill So Far",
    x_axis_label="Table",
    y_axis_label="Total Bill ($)",
    height=350,
)
p.step(list(range(1, 21)), running_max.tolist(), mode="after", line_width=2)

maidr.show(p)  #<<
```

### Heatmap

```{python}
#| warning: false
#| fig-alt: Heatmap of airline passengers by month and year

import seaborn as sns
from bokeh.plotting import figure
from bokeh.transform import linear_cmap

import maidr  #<<

flights = sns.load_dataset("flights")
flights["year"] = flights["year"].astype(str)
flights["month"] = flights["month"].astype(str)
years = sorted(flights["year"].unique())
months = flights["month"].unique().tolist()[::-1]

p = figure(
    x_range=years,
    y_range=months,
    title="Airline Passengers by Month and Year",
    x_axis_label="Year",
    y_axis_label="Month",
    height=450,
)
cells = p.rect(
    x="year", y="month", width=1, height=1, source=flights, line_color=None,
    fill_color=linear_cmap(
        "passengers", "Viridis256",
        flights["passengers"].min(), flights["passengers"].max(),
    ),
)
p.add_layout(cells.construct_color_bar(title="Passengers"), "right")

maidr.show(p)  #<<
```

### Pie Chart

```{python}
#| warning: false
#| fig-alt: Pie chart of the number of penguins of each species

from math import pi

import seaborn as sns
from bokeh.models import ColumnDataSource
from bokeh.plotting import figure
from bokeh.transform import cumsum

import maidr  #<<

penguins = sns.load_dataset("penguins")
counts = penguins["species"].value_counts().sort_index()
source = ColumnDataSource(
    {
        "species": counts.index.tolist(),
        "penguins": counts.tolist(),
        "angle": (counts / counts.sum() * 2 * pi).tolist(),
        "color": ["#4c72b0", "#dd8452", "#55a868"],
    }
)

p = figure(title="Penguins by Species", height=350, toolbar_location=None)
p.wedge(
    x=0, y=1, radius=0.4, source=source,
    start_angle=cumsum("angle", include_zero=True), end_angle=cumsum("angle"),
    line_color="white", fill_color="color", legend_field="species",
)
p.axis.visible = False
p.grid.visible = False

maidr.show(p)  #<<
```

Each slice is announced with the value it was computed from -- here the
`penguins` column, which the angles are proportional to -- and named by the
legend. The right arrow walks the pie clockwise, as for every pie in
**maidr**, so on a pie Bokeh drew counterclockwise from 3 o'clock it starts on
the slice drawn last.

### Candlestick Chart

```{python}
#| warning: false
#| fig-alt: Candlestick chart of fifteen trading days of a simulated stock price

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from bokeh.plotting import figure

import maidr  #<<

rng = np.random.default_rng(4)
dates = pd.bdate_range("2024-03-01", periods=15)
close = (100 + rng.normal(0, 1.5, len(dates)).cumsum()).round(2)
open_ = np.r_[100.0, close[:-1]]
df = pd.DataFrame(
    {
        "date": dates,
        "open": open_,
        "close": close,
        "high": (np.maximum(open_, close) + rng.uniform(0.2, 1.5, len(dates))).round(2),
        "low": (np.minimum(open_, close) - rng.uniform(0.2, 1.5, len(dates))).round(2),
    }
)
inc = df.close > df.open
dec = df.open > df.close
w = 12 * 60 * 60 * 1000  # half a day, in ms

p = figure(
    x_axis_type="datetime",
    title="Simulated Stock, March 2024",
    x_axis_label="Date",
    y_axis_label="Price ($)",
    height=350,
)
p.segment(df.date, df.high, df.date, df.low, color="black")
p.vbar(df.date[dec], w, df.open[dec], df.close[dec], color="#c44e52")
p.vbar(df.date[inc], w, df.open[inc], df.close[inc], fill_color="white",
       line_color="#55a868", line_width=2)

maidr.show(p)  #<<
```

This is Bokeh's own candlestick recipe: a `segment` from each day's high to
its low and a `vbar` between its open and close, one renderer for rising days
and one for falling. **maidr** reads them together as one candlestick, a
candle per date. A body is drawn between two prices whichever is larger, so
**maidr** needs to be told which one is the open: here the prices are passed
straight through (`top=open`, `bottom=close`), which draws a rising day's body
upside down and says so; a source with `open` and `close` columns says so
too. Bodies drawn the right way up with neither are not guessed at, and are
read as bars. A day that closes exactly where it opened gets no body from this
recipe, so its open and close are not in the figure: **maidr** leaves that
day out, with a warning.

### Multi-Panel Layout (gridplot)

```{python}
#| warning: false
#| fig-alt: Two panels side by side, a bar chart of penguins per species and a line of passengers per year

import seaborn as sns
from bokeh.layouts import gridplot
from bokeh.plotting import figure

import maidr  #<<

penguins = sns.load_dataset("penguins")
flights = sns.load_dataset("flights")
counts = penguins["species"].value_counts().sort_index()
per_year = flights.groupby("year")["passengers"].sum()

left = figure(
    x_range=counts.index.tolist(), title="Penguins per Species",
    x_axis_label="Species", y_axis_label="Penguins", width=350, height=300,
)
left.vbar(x=counts.index.tolist(), top=counts.tolist(), width=0.8)

right = figure(
    title="Passengers per Year", x_axis_label="Year",
    y_axis_label="Passengers", width=350, height=300,
)
right.line(per_year.index.tolist(), per_year.tolist(), line_width=2)

maidr.show(gridplot([[left, right]]))  #<<
```

Each figure of a `gridplot`, `row` or `column` is a subplot. Press
<kbd>Enter</kbd> to go into one, <kbd>Escape</kbd> to come back out, and the
arrow keys between them, in the directions they are laid out on the page. A
figure with nothing **maidr** can read is left out of the grid.

### Stacked Area Plot [experimental]

```{python}
#| warning: false
#| fig-alt: Stacked area chart of monthly passengers in 1958, 1959 and 1960

import seaborn as sns
from bokeh.plotting import figure

import maidr  #<<

flights = sns.load_dataset("flights")
wide = flights.pivot(index="month", columns="year", values="passengers")
source = {
    "month": list(range(1, 13)),
    "1958": wide[1958].tolist(),
    "1959": wide[1959].tolist(),
    "1960": wide[1960].tolist(),
}

p = figure(
    title="Monthly Passengers, 1958 to 1960",
    x_axis_label="Month",
    y_axis_label="Passengers",
    height=350,
)
p.varea_stack(
    ["1958", "1959", "1960"],
    x="month",
    source=source,
    color=["#4c72b0", "#55a868", "#c44e52"],
    legend_label=["1958", "1959", "1960"],
)
p.legend.location = "top_left"

maidr.show(p)  #<<
```

### Horizontal Area Plot [experimental]

```{python}
#| warning: false
#| fig-alt: Sideways area chart of airline passengers by month in 1960, the months running down the page

import seaborn as sns
from bokeh.plotting import figure

import maidr  #<<

flights = sns.load_dataset("flights")
months = flights[flights["year"] == 1960]

p = figure(
    title="Passengers by Month, 1960",
    x_axis_label="Passengers",
    y_axis_label="Month",
    height=400,
)
p.harea(
    y=list(range(1, 13)), x1=0, x2=months["passengers"].tolist(),
    fill_color="#8172b3", fill_alpha=0.7,
)

maidr.show(p)  #<<
```

An `harea` is read as the same area on its side: the arrow keys step through
the months, and the passengers are what you hear.

### Gantt Chart [experimental]

```{python}
#| warning: false
#| fig-alt: Gantt chart of a five-task project plan across January 2024

import pandas as pd
from bokeh.models import ColumnDataSource
from bokeh.plotting import figure

import maidr  #<<

plan = pd.DataFrame(
    {
        "task": ["Research", "Design", "Build", "Test", "Launch"],
        "start": pd.to_datetime(
            ["2024-01-01", "2024-01-08", "2024-01-15", "2024-01-24", "2024-01-30"]
        ),
        "end": pd.to_datetime(
            ["2024-01-10", "2024-01-17", "2024-01-26", "2024-01-31", "2024-02-02"]
        ),
    }
)

p = figure(
    y_range=plan["task"].tolist()[::-1],
    x_axis_type="datetime",
    title="Project Plan, January 2024",
    x_axis_label="Date",
    y_axis_label="Task",
    height=300,
)
p.hbar(
    y="task", left="start", right="end", height=0.6,
    source=ColumnDataSource(plan), color="#4c72b0",
)

maidr.show(p)  #<<
```

An `hbar` running from one date to another is read as a Gantt chart: each
task is a lane, the up and down arrows move between lanes as they are drawn,
and every bar is announced with its start and end dates and its length in
days.

### Hexbin Plot [experimental]

```{python}
#| warning: false
#| fig-alt: Hexbin plot of penguin flipper length against body mass

import seaborn as sns
from bokeh.plotting import figure

import maidr  #<<

penguins = sns.load_dataset("penguins").dropna()
flipper = (penguins["flipper_length_mm"] - 200) / 10
mass = (penguins["body_mass_g"] - 4200) / 800

p = figure(
    title="Flipper Length vs Body Mass (standardised)",
    x_axis_label="Flipper Length (x10 mm from 200)",
    y_axis_label="Body Mass (x800 g from 4200)",
    match_aspect=True,
    height=400,
)
tiles, bins = p.hexbin(flipper.to_numpy(), mass.to_numpy(), size=0.3)
p.add_layout(tiles.construct_color_bar(title="Penguins"), "right")

maidr.show(p)  #<<
```

Each hexagon is a bin announced by its centre and how many penguins fell in
it; the up and down arrows move to the nearest bin of the staggered row above
or below.

## Saving and embedding

`maidr.save_html(p, "chart.html")` writes the same page to a file.
`use_cdn` decides where `maidr.js` comes from, exactly as for matplotlib and
Plotly; BokehJS itself is always loaded from Bokeh's CDN at the version you
have installed, as plotly.js is from Plotly's, so opening the page needs a
network connection either way.
